subject.title: Bug:  ignores  config and returns success on media failure

question: Should Feishu outbound media support a persistent configured local-root allowlist, or should allowlist violations remain fail-closed with explicit staging guidance?
rationale: This changes both host filesystem read/upload scope and user-visible delivery semantics, so code inspection can prove the bug but cannot choose the security/product contract.

options.title: Use shared root policy first
options.body: Adopt or design the shared filesystem/media-root contract, then wire Feishu to that policy and make allowlist failures visibly non-successful.

options.title: Fail closed with guidance only
options.body: Do not add Feishu-specific roots; instead make local allowlist violations fail clearly and document the managed staging directories.

options.title: Add Feishu-specific roots
options.body: Allow `channels.feishu.mediaLocalRoots` directly, but require explicit security docs and tests for host file read/upload boundaries.

recommendation.title: Use shared root policy first
recommendation.body: Adopt or design the shared filesystem/media-root contract, then wire Feishu to that policy and make allowlist failures visibly non-successful.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the most recent current-line outbound/media plumbing and authored the shared media access refactor this decision depends on.
